round_two_note: My round-one vote turned on one fact: how much mineral inventory exists beyond the 206,473 MMcfe proved book. The targeted research returned that question unresolved - no artifact in the packet carries net royalty acres, undrilled locations, or operator permit activity. It did surface one piece of directional support I had not isolated: pro forma volumes fell only 4.4% against a producing book that implies 13.14% to 13.75% decline, so roughly 9 points of annual volume is already being replaced by new wells converting inventory. That confirms unbooked inventory exists and is being drilled. It does not size what remains, so my position is unchanged.

explanatory_strength.rationale: Unchanged from round one. The contract states the economic claim in the right units, applies the OpCo economic interest before the per-share division, refuses to deduct claims already serviced inside CAFD, and partitions the proved book so no molecule is valued twice. The research loop surfaced nothing that weakens the explanation; the one new datum, an unreflected $6.3m April 2026 Senior Notes prepayment, is a small favourable correction to senior claims worth about $0.23 per share. Still short of 5 because the structure remains a perpetuity approximation of a finite book rather than a period-by-period distribution curve.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Unchanged, and now demonstrated rather than suspected. The research loop asked the packet three decision-material questions and it answered one partially and two not at all. There is no acreage census, no comparable-transaction evidence, and no independent adversarial examination of the name. Combined with the absence of any 10-Q or 10-K since the 2026-06-10 IPO, this packet cannot support a decision in either direction on the variable that matters most to my lens.

downside_control.rationale: Held at 2. The credit facts recovered in the research loop are genuinely better than I assumed - the Senior Notes rate fell from Adjusted Term SOFR + 6.50% to + 4.75%, maturity extended to 2031-05-20, the revolver is undrawn, and debt fell from $231.425m to $75.0m or possibly $68.7m at the IPO. But my downside concern was never solvency; it was that the distribution is undeclared, the producing book runs 7.27 years, and royalty revenue is an unhedged pass-through with no operating lever. None of that moved.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Unchanged. At $26.16 against a base of $5.71 the contract computes negative 19.53% annualised over seven years and no case in the range is positive. The unquantified acreage could only improve this, but an unmeasured option is not a return, and buying it at roughly 2.7x PV-10 means paying for it in full before it is sized.

claims.claim: Unbooked mineral inventory exists and is materially offsetting decline, but remains unquantified in this packet.
claims.evidence: research_response.json q1: pro forma volumes fell 4.4% (67,255 to 64,270 Mcfe/d) against a 13.14%-13.75% implied producing decline; no acreage, location or permit data in any packet artifact.

claims.claim: The contract's senior_claims figure of $95.106m is modestly overstated.
claims.evidence: research_response.json q2: the as-adjusted $75.0m debt does not reflect a voluntary $6.3m Senior Notes prepayment made in April 2026.

claims.claim: No independent party has examined this name.
claims.evidence: research_response.json q3: the frozen cross-check indexes zero sources and the frozen adversarial pass reconciled no filings and scanned no disclosures.

claims.claim: The two legs of the routed method are both evidenced and mutually non-overlapping.
claims.evidence: valuation_contract.json component_coverage reports 2 additive components and no double_counting_flags; the partition splits 178,544 MMcfe producing from 27,930 MMcfe non-producing.

strongest_counter_explanation: Unchanged and now the explicit open item. WhiteHawk holds minerals in fee, so its economic life is not the 8.4-year proved reserve life but however long EQT, Antero, Range and CNX keep drilling the acreage - on Appalachian inventory, decades. Proved reserves are a booking convention bounded by SEC rules and the five-year PUD window, not an inventory census, and the 4.4% observed volume decline against a 13.75% producing decline is direct evidence that the convention understates the asset. If that is right the correct model is a perpetual royalty on a drilling program, 2.7x PV-10 is an ordinary multiple for a mineral company with long unbooked inventory, and this contract's base is far too low.
most_important_missing_fact: A quantification of unbooked mineral inventory - net royalty acres by play with undrilled location counts and operator permit or rig activity against them. The research loop confirmed this cannot be answered from the frozen packet and it must come from the first 10-K's Business section or an acreage census.
falsifiers: An acreage and undrilled-location census showing inventory large enough to sustain volumes flat for a decade, which would falsify the finite-life framing this contract rests on.
The first 10-Q reporting net production above 67,255 Mcfe/d, implying a producing decline shallower than the reserve report supports.
The FY2026 reserve report raising PV-10 above $500m, resetting the unit value both components are built on.
specialist_findings: The scarce-asset lens's required evidence is now half satisfied: non-overlapping physical inventory and unit economics are established, realization timing is proxied by a haircut band rather than a schedule, and remaining owner capital is clean. The legal economic claim is established for the proved book only.
PV-10 and the owner-cash component's base required return are both 10%, so the two legs are discount-rate comparable rather than accidentally divergent.

The realization haircut of 0.40/0.55/0.70 on the 27,930 MMcfe of non-producing volumes remains the weakest judgment in the contract, standing in for a schedule of when those volumes come online that no filed document provides.

The research loop is itself the finding: a packet that cannot answer two of three decision-material questions is not a decision-grade evidence set for this lens, whatever the contract's status field says.
